$comment: Permissions for the unattended 'Daily job-board scrape (pestidev)' cloud routine.
The routine's stored prompt asserts that a scoped rule for the two curl calls already
exists in .claude/settings.local.json. It did not — this repo contained only prompt.txt.
Note settings.local.json is the wrong filename for this anyway: a routine gets a fresh
checkout, so only a COMMITTED settings file reaches it, and *.local is conventionally
Why Bash(curl:*) is broad rather than pinned to bakan7.netlify.app:
Bash rules match on literal command PREFIX, and prompt.txt's own examples vary the
invocation (-d inline vs -d @file.json). A pinned prefix would deny a legitimate call
mid-run, and a run whose POST never fires produces nothing at all. The blast radius is
bounded by the token itself: AI_INGEST_TOKEN is deliberately low-privilege (see
AI_SCRAPER_PLAN.md section 0 in Andrssss/MyWebsite) — it reaches only the filtered
ai-registry / ai-ingest / ai-deactivate endpoints, never the ~30 background scrapers
that CRON_SECRET authorizes. The API re-applies its own deterministic filters on top.
git push/commit are denied: the current design has NO git output — the API POST is the
only output. The superseded registry-file design pushed to main and failed silently on
every run from 2026-07-17 onward, so not one finding ever reached the DB.
